title: State of Bilateral Relations with Malaysia following 9th Malaysia-Singapore Leaders' Retreat
what_it_is: State of Bilateral Relations with Malaysia following 9th Malaysia-Singapore Leaders' Retreat

sections.label: Bilateral relations with Malaysia update
sections.summary: A question asks the Foreign Minister for an update on bilateral relations with Malaysia after the 9th Leaders' Retreat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs whether he can provide an update on the state of bilateral relations with Malaysia following the 9th Malaysia-Singapore Leaders' Retreat.

sections.label: Suspension of overlapping port limits
sections.summary: Both sides agreed on de-escalation measures on 14 March 2019 and mutually suspended overlapping port limits, applying pre-25 October and pre-6 December 2018 limits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Malaysian Foreign Minister Mr Saifuddin Abdullah and I agreed on a set of measures to de-escalate tensions on 14 March 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Malaysia and Singapore have, therefore, mutually suspended the implementation of the overlapping port limits, and we have applied the port limits that were in effect prior to 25 October 2018 and 6 December 2018 respectively.

sections.label: Pasir Gudang and Seletar Airport measures
sections.summary: On 6 April 2019 both sides agreed Malaysia would indefinitely suspend its Restricted Area over Pasir Gudang and Singapore would withdraw Seletar ILS procedures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: On 6 April 2019, both sides agreed for Malaysia to indefinitely suspend its Restricted Area over Pasir Gudang, and for Singapore to withdraw the Instrument Landing System (ILS) procedures for Seletar Airport.

sections.label: RTS Link and HSR suspension
sections.summary: Singapore will consider Malaysia's proposal to suspend the RTS Link for six months from 1 April 2019, similar to the HSR suspension up to 31 May 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: On land connectivity, Singapore will consider Malaysia’s proposal to suspend the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link Project for six months from 1 April 2019 and we will do so in a manner that is similar to the arrangements that we made for the suspension of the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail (HSR) Project.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: As for the HSR Project, both sides had earlier agreed to suspend the Project up to 31 May 2020.

sections.label: Hope for projects way forward
sections.summary: The ball is in Malaysia's court, and Singapore hopes Malaysia will find a way forward in the projects within the requested suspension period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The ball is now in their court, and we hope that Malaysia will find a way forward in the projects within the period of suspension that they have requested.

sections.label: Johor water supply and pollution
sections.summary: Johor will need more water, but the biggest threat to its water supply is lack of environmental protection, with seven pollution episodes since 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Quite apart from Johor's own growing needs, and we expect that as we do more together with Johor, and as our bilateral projects take off and the economy improves, Johor will need more water.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But actually, and here I would be very frank, the biggest threat to Johor's own water supply is actually the lack of environmental protection.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The seven episodes of pollution since 2017, which resulted in the water treatment plants having to be shut down, are a clear and present amber warning light.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singaporeans may not have noticed because whenever our plant shuts down, fortunately, because of very careful and astute management by PUB, Singaporeans' water supply is apparently not affected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But every time our plant in Johor shuts down, there is disruption and water rationing in Johor.

sections.label: Linggiu Reservoir dam construction
sections.summary: The dam over the Linggiu River created the Linggiu Reservoir, operating since the 1990s, which helps ensure good yield from the Johor River.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: A clear example of this is the construction of the dam over the Linggiu River, which has led to the development of the Linggiu Reservoir, which has been operating since the 1990s, and has been a significant buffer that has helped to ensure good yield from the Johor River.

sections.label: Singapore investments in Linggiu Reservoir
sections.summary: Singapore estimates it has spent over $1 billion on such projects, and the Linggiu Reservoir investments are owned by Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In fact, our estimate is that, over the years, we have probably spent over $1 billion on such projects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I should also add that these investments that we have made in Linggiu Reservoir, ultimately, they are owned by Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And just as in 2011 when we returned all the waterworks in full working order to Johor – these were the waterworks in Tebrau, Skudai and Gunung Pulai, which were pursuant to the 1961 Water Agreement – we intend to do the same thing pursuant to the current 1962 Water Agreement, which expires in 2061.
